chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie, from Salih ibn Uqba, from Yazeed ibn Abdul Malik, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who passed by while he was in Ihram, so he seized an antelope, milked it, and drank its milk. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon him is blood (of a sacrificial animal), and a penalty in the Haram.'

key_terms.إِحْرَام: The state of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.دَم: A sacrificial animal offered as expiation
key_terms.ظَبْيَة: An antelope (a type of wild animal)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for milking and drinking the milk of a wild animal while in Ihram?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies that milking a wild animal while in Ihram incurs both a sacrificial expiation (dam) and a specific penalty (jaza) if it occurs within the Haram boundaries. Shia jurists utilize this to distinguish between the general prohibition of hunting and the specific liabilities arising from utilizing the animal's produce, emphasizing the sanctity of the sacred precincts. The ruling underscores the principle that Ihram restrictions extend beyond mere capture to include beneficial use of wild fauna.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Muhammad Bin Ismail Bin Bazie, from Salih Bin Uqba, from Yazeed Bin Abdul Malik,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws regarding a man passing-by and he is in Ihraam. So he seizes an antelope, so he milks it and drinks its milk. Heasws said: ‘Upon him is blood (of a sacrificial animal), and a penalty in the Harram’.
en.sarwar: 13. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn from ‘Isma‘il ibn Bazi’ from Salih ibn ‘Uqbah from Yazid ibn ‘ Abd al-Malik who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who in the state of Ihram, when passing by takes hold of a deer, draws her milk and drinks it. He (the Imam) said, ‘He owes an animal offering as penalty to offer in al-Haram (the sacred area).”’
